summary.headline: Crizac Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% YoY to INR2,012 million on adverse university mix; management now guides FY27 flat versus FY26.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR2,012 million, down 4% YoY and below the INR3,917 million of Q4 FY26, consistent with Q1 being the seasonal trough. Management attributed the decline to a less favourable university mix (fewer high-fee top-ranked university bonuses and slabs), not lower platform activity, as enrolments rose 15% YoY. EBITDA fell 7.6% YoY to INR600 million, with margin at 29.8% versus 31%, while PAT grew 2.9% to INR471 million. Management moved from earlier growth expectations to a flat FY27 outlook, citing flight disruption and rupee volatility expected to hit Q2, with pent-up demand expected in Q3 and Q4. It also announced a leadership change: Chairman Christopher Nagle stepped down as UK CEO and became Non-Executive Chairman of the Indian holding company, with Eric Wijmenga taking UK and Europe operations.

financial_highlights.change: -4% YoY (constant currency); below Q4 FY26 INR3,917 million
-7.6% YoY from INR649 million; margin 29.8% vs 31% in Q1 FY26; up 585 bps QoQ from 24% in Q4 FY26
vs INR4.0 lakh FY26 and INR3.55 lakh FY24 (analyst's division, not company-stated)

segments.name: UK (largest destination)
segments.commentary: Management says UK share of total student visas granted rose from 3.5% in FY24 to 6% in FY26; UK concentration still around 97% per analyst, with a target to go below 60% within about three years.

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: US share of Indian student visas rose from 9% to 13.9%, though management described the US visa environment as restrictive and its planned expansion as stalled.

segments.name: Acquisitions (acquired businesses)
segments.commentary: Acquired businesses contributed around INR6 crore of revenue in Q1; Innova Consultancy (acquired July 2026) is under INR7 crore in size and adds Mexico source and Netherlands destination.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and performance expected broadly flat versus FY26 ("same line as last year"); earlier informal 15-17% growth view withdrawn.
Q2 FY27 expected to be down, due to flight cancellations (February-June) and rupee volatility affecting April-June intakes.
Recovery expected in Q3 and Q4 from pent-up demand; management said Q3 application flow is healthy.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected in the 25%-27% range, per analyst question and management confirmation.
Value-added services (ForeignAdmits: education financing, visa prep, accommodation, forex loans) expected to add 2-5% to EBITDA and 1-1.5% of revenue over next couple of years.
Consolidated PBT to benefit from UK investments; management expects the effect in Q3.
Dividend policy: minimum 40% of PAT for at least three years per DRHP, with FY26 already paid.
capex_capacity: Investing in people and infrastructure for technology and AI; management said benefits will build progressively, with upfront cost.
Acquired ForeignAdmits (June 2026), an education financing and visa preparation platform; founder Nikhil Jain joined as Chief Product and Marketing Officer.
Acquired 100% of Innova Consultancy Limited in July 2026 via wholly owned UK subsidiary; integration ongoing. Both recent acquisitions were each under INR10 crore in cost, per management.
Recent deals also include Studies Planet (Latin America), Global Tree (India), Medway (New Zealand) and EduMentor (talent acquisition).
demand_pricing: Revenue per student fell in Q1 due to university mix: fewer high-fee top-ranked universities, with missed bonuses and slabs. Management said per-university realisations are unchanged.

Top 3 universities were 41% of Q1 revenue per management's/analyst's figures; management said Q1 is skewed because few universities have April-June intakes, and top 10 universities contribute roughly 60-70% on a full-year basis.
Conversion rate about 10% of unique applicants; TTM blended conversion said to be around 10%.
Unique applicants were about 47,000 in Q1; a student typically applies to 2-2.5 universities.
Platform covers 450+ university partners, 12 destination markets, 85+ source markets; management said it represents more than 95 of 100 UK commercial universities.
Competition: incumbents in other English-speaking markets make expansion slower; management cited US policy changes as blocking planned US expansion.

Visa and currency pressure: UK graduate route cut from 24 to 18 months; US/UK strength in currency raising costs for emerging-market students; demand redirecting to Ireland, Germany and New Zealand per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue fall QoQ and what is the Q2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency revenue fell about 4% as volume rose 15% but university mix shifted; Q2 expected weaker due to Feb-June flight cancellations and rupee volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be 20-25% or 15-17% as earlier hinted?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management now expects FY27 flat versus FY26, with pent-up demand in Q3 and Q4 offsetting Q1 and Q2 shortfalls.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone PBT above consolidated PBT in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Crizac India standalone recognised some payments as revenue; investments in Crizac UK and subsidiaries should pay off in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a buyback plan given the stock trades around 11x EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has only about 20% public float and SEBI rules do not allow a buyback at this level; the compliance team will look at the suggestion.

qa_highlights.question: Will the UK concentration fall, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the target is to get UK share below 60% within about three years, aided by Innova (Netherlands) and other markets, though policy shifts will slow this.

qa_highlights.question: Will value-added services become material?
qa_highlights.answer: Not initially; they could add 2-5% to EBITDA and 1-1.5% of revenue over the next couple of years, with ForeignAdmits accelerating this.

qa_highlights.question: Is the dividend a one-time payout?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the DRHP commits to a minimum 40% of PAT as dividend for at least three years; FY26 is done, leaving at least two more years.
